utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hello Danielle. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: A bit off actually. I stopped taking my Lexapro about two weeks ago. I just felt like I didn't need it anymore and I didn't want to wait to discuss it with my psychiatrist.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: It sounds like you're feeling more confident in yourself. What made you feel ready to try without the medication?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I just felt stable and wanted to try. But honestly this week has been rough. I've had new symptoms — I'm really irritable and dizzy. I didn't connect it to the medication until just now.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Irritability can stem from so many sources — stress, diet, sleep. Let's explore what's been happening in your life that might be contributing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I mean life is fine otherwise. I started taking a new herbal supplement too, ashwagandha and something else. My friend recommended it and I figured why not.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Natural remedies can be a great complement to therapy. It's good that you're exploring options. How has your sleep been?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Okay actually. But I had a panic attack on Tuesday. Out of nowhere. That hasn't happened in months. New symptom, nothing like that has happened recently.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Panic attacks can return during stressful periods. Let's practice some grounding techniques you can use when that happens.
